robot.name: Clone Alpha
robot.status_notes: Clone Robotics has opened limited reservations for the first 279 units, but no complete Alpha has been publicly demonstrated. Protoclone V1 was shown hanging in a workshop video in February 2025. Company roadmap targets 2028 for first commercial products. No price or delivery date published.
intended_use_cases: household chores (sandwich making, laundry, vacuuming, dishwashing)
personal assistance (following, holding items, retrieving items)

height.notes: Height not published in reviewed sources.

weight.notes: Weight not published in reviewed sources.

payload.notes: Payload not published in reviewed sources.

runtime.notes: Third-party Alibaba buying guide states current prototypes sustain about 1.5 hours per charge; not an official spec.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: TechEBlog reports Protoclone with '200+ degrees of freedom'; other sources state 164 DoF in upper body alone. Total DoF for full Alpha not officially confirmed.

walking_speed.notes: Walking speed not published; company claims 'walks naturally' but no speed.

hands.description: Clone Hand with Myofiber artificial muscles. Reports vary: 26 degrees of freedom in each hand/wrist/elbow (Protoclone) and 27 DoF for standalone Clone Hand. Human-level grip force claimed.
hands.force_feedback: 320 pressure sensors provide force feedback (company claim)

compute.description: NVIDIA Jetson Thor GPU (reported). Runs Clone's 'Cybernet' visuomotor foundation model; edge-localized AI (company claim).

actuators.description: Myofiber water-powered artificial muscles. Company claims: response <50 ms, >30% unloaded contraction, at least 1 kg force per 3 g fiber. Protoclone reported with over 1,000 Myofibers. Hydraulic pump: 500W, 40 SLPM at 100 psi.

availability.notes: Official page accepts reservations for first 279 units. No official price. Media mentions $20,000 target (not confirmed). No retail channel; B2B only per Alibaba guide.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Clone claims human-level finger strength. Component demos include hand and torso (video titles only). Tasks listed include sandwich making, laundry, but no full Alpha demo shown.
caveats: No full Alpha manipulation demo; video titles unverified; no success rates.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: No autonomous task execution demonstrated. Telekinesis training platform described but no execution shown.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Company claims 'walks naturally' but no public walking demo. Protoclone shown hanging only. Roadmap targets 2027 for natural walking.
caveats: No walking speed or demonstration; company claim only.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Sensors include 4 depth cameras, 70 inertial, 320 pressure; runs Cybernet visuomotor model. No scene understanding demo.

human_interaction.summary: Company claims natural language interface ('speak to Clone in plain English') and witty dialogue via Telekinesis.

endurance_reliability.summary: No reliability data. Third-party guide states ~1.5 hours runtime; no endurance testing published.
caveats: Runtime from unofficial source; no MTBF or failure data.

human_environment_fit.summary: Company claims soft, plush, featherweight, won't damage floor. No safety certification.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: No named customer deployments. Only limited reservations open (279 units).

accessibility_value.summary: Reservation page exists but no price or delivery date. $20,000 target mentioned in media, not official.

evidence_items.title: Clone Alpha official reservation page
evidence_items.claim: Clone Robotics accepts reservations for the first 279 Alpha Edition units; Myofiber specs include <50 ms response, >30% contraction, 1 kg force per 3 g fiber.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines artificial muscle performance and reservation availability.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Reserve one of the first 279 Clones ever made, in its Alpha Edition.
evidence_items.source_location: Clone Robotics Android product page, hero section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company spec page; Myofiber metrics not independently measured.

evidence_items.title: Protoclone unveiling specs
evidence_items.claim: TechEBlog reports Protoclone has 200+ degrees of freedom, over 1,000 Myofibers, and more than 200 sensors; pre-orders set to begin later in 2025, no price announced.
evidence_items.notes: Media report of company claims; prototype only.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Provides quantitative DoF and sensor counts from a secondary source.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: This anatomically accurate robot is essentially a synthetic human with 200+ degrees of freedom, over 1,000 Myofibers, and more than 200 sensors.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Secondary source; numbers not confirmed by Clone Robotics directly.

evidence_items.title: Orders opened and task list
evidence_items.claim: Clone Robotics opened limited orders for Alpha; Telekinesis training platform teaches skills like shaking hands, pouring drinks, making sandwiches, laundry, vacuuming, dishwashing, and witty dialogue.
evidence_items.notes: Thomasnet video transcript; company marketing claims.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Lists intended household capabilities, but no demonstration shown.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The robots come with the Telekinesis training platform that’s used to learn and master skills like shaking hands, pouring drinks, making sandwiches, doing laundry, vacuuming floors, turning on and off lights, setting the table, loading and unloading the dishwasher, and firing off some witty dialogue.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Marketing language; no task execution demonstrated.

evidence_items.title: Sensor and vascular specs
evidence_items.claim: Alpha has 4 depth cameras in skull, 70 inertial sensors, 320 pressure sensors, and a 500-watt pump delivering 40 SLPM.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines perception hardware and hydraulic power.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: It relies on 4 depth cameras in the skull for vision, 70 inertial sensors that sense the body’s position and movement, and 320 pressure sensors that provide force feedback.
evidence_items.source_location: Thomasnet article, 'Alpha’s artificial nervous system' section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Specs from company, not independently verified.

evidence_items.title: Runtime and pricing from buying guide
evidence_items.claim: Alibaba.com guide states current Clone Alpha prototypes sustain ~1.5 hours per charge, target price $20,000, B2B only, Clone Hand starts at $2,800.
evidence_items.notes: Third-party buying guide; not official specs.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Only runtime figure found, but low reliability.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Current prototypes sustain ~1.5 hours per charge — insufficient for shift-long operation.
evidence_items.source_location: Alibaba.com buying guide, table row 'Runtime & Endurance'
evidence_items.verification_notes: Directory content; may be inaccurate or based on early prototypes.

evidence_items.title: No complete Alpha demonstrated
evidence_items.claim: Scribd article notes Clone has yet to publicly demonstrate a complete Alpha robot in action; preorders open for 279 units; upper body 164 points, 26 DoF hand/wrist/elbow.
evidence_items.notes: Republished article from Maginative; content dated Dec 5, 2024.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Confirms prototype status and lack of full demonstration.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: However, potential customers and industry observers should note that Clone has yet to publicly demonstrate a complete Alpha robot in action.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Secondary source; statement as of late 2024.

evidence_items.title: Upper body DoF details
evidence_items.claim: Impact Lab reports upper torso has 164 DoF including 20 shoulder, 6 per vertebra, 26 hand/wrist/elbow; uses NVIDIA Jetson Thor and Cybernet visuomotor model.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The robot's upper torso offers 164 degrees of freedom, including 20 degrees in the shoulder, 6 degrees of movement per vertebra in the spine, and 26 degrees in the hand, wrist, and elbow.
evidence_items.source_location: Impact Lab article, paragraph on upper torso

evidence_items.title: Vascular system pump specs
evidence_items.claim: Impact Lab reports a 500-watt pump delivers 40 SLPM at 100 psi; Aquajet valves operate under 1 watt.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: The robot's vascular system, mimicking the human circulatory system, is powered by a compact, 500-watt electric pump that delivers 40 SLPM at 100 psi, closely resembling the function of a human heart.
evidence_items.source_location: Impact Lab article, vascular system paragraph

evidence_items.title: Missing disclosures
evidence_items.claim: No height, weight, payload, walking speed, battery capacity, or official price were found in reviewed sources.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Judges should reduce confidence on specs and value.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Gaps identified across all reviewed primary and secondary sources.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Absence of disclosure, not evidence of inability.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Clone Alpha is a prototype bipedal humanoid with unique Myofiber artificial muscles. No complete robot has been publicly demonstrated, and all specs and capabilities are company claims or media reports. Evidence is thin and mostly tier 1.
strongest_positive_evidence: Official reservation page confirms 279-unit limited edition.
Detailed upper-body DoF and sensor specs reported consistently.
Company claims natural language and household tasks via Telekinesis (unverified).
Multiple YouTube videos exist, but no content assessed.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No full Alpha demonstration; Protoclone shown hanging only.
No height, weight, payload, walking speed, or battery capacity.
No price or delivery date; $20,000 is media target only.
No independent verification of Myofiber performance or runtime.
conflicting_claims: Total DoF: 200+ (TechEBlog) vs 164 upper body only (multiple sources); not clearly reconciled.
Hand DoF: 26 per hand/wrist/elbow (Scribd) vs 27 DoF standalone Clone Hand (Alibaba).
Runtime: ~1.5 hours from Alibaba guide, but no other source; not official.
Announcement date: Thomasnet article Jan 3 2025 vs Scribd content Dec 5 2024; used earliest.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit walking or task execution; no demonstration exists.
Do not treat $20,000 as official price.
Do not use video titles as evidence of capabilities.
Do not infer total DoF from conflicting reports without caveat.

currentness.currentness_notes: Clone Alpha is the current full-body humanoid prototype from Clone Robotics as of 2026-10-29. Torso 4 shown in video title but no details. No new full robot announced.

excluded_claims.reason: No video or description of walking; only hanging shown in TechEBlog article.
Only mentioned in media and buying guide as target; no official listing.
Only from Alibaba buying guide, not Clone Robotics.
Multiple sources confirm no complete Alpha shown.
No evidence of autonomy; Telekinesis described but not shown.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Clone Alpha is Clone Robotics' prototype bipedal humanoid that uses water-powered Myofiber artificial muscles instead of electric motors. The company accepts reservations for 279 units but has not demonstrated a complete robot. Specs (200+ DoF, 4 depth cameras, 70 inertial sensors, 320 pressure sensors, NVIDIA Jetson Thor) come from media reports. No walking, task execution, or autonomy has been shown. A $20,000 target price is mentioned but not official. Evidence is weak and primarily company claims at tier 1.
strongest_evidence: Official reservation page for 279 Alpha Edition units.
Detailed sensor and actuator specs reported by multiple secondary sources.
Company roadmap with target dates (torso 2026, walking 2027, commercial 2028).
weakest_evidence: No official physical specs (height, weight, payload, speed, battery).
Runtime figure from low-reliability directory only.
known_do_not_credit: Task execution or household chores (not shown).
Total DoF as 200+ without caveat (conflicting 164 upper body).
